newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, Eurodollars seen creeping higher.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, Eurodollars seen creeping higher.

text.p: Japanese and U.S. interest-rate futures had a listless session on SIMEX on Tuesday as a holiday in Japan and the absence of some local players after an extended weekend hampered interest, dealers said.
But they said the Euroyen and Eurodollar futures showed potential for further gains amid confidence short-term interest rates would be held steady in both countries in the foreseeable future.
"We saw some strength in the Euroyen in the last few days and it could reach up higher towards the end of the week," said a trader with a U.S. futures house.
He added, however, that September Euroyen would have trouble clearing 99.40. It was quoted at 99.38 at 1115 GMT against its IMM close at 99.37 on light volume of 294 lots.
The front months, March and June, saw greater volume but remained practically static all day.
Japanese government bond futures were not traded due to the Japanese holiday.
June Eurodollars ended unchanged at 94.35 against their IMM close and September also unchanged at 94.22.
Dealers said interest would be focused on the U.S. Producer Price Index for January, due to be released on Friday.
"I think we're on an upward trend for the short-term but the Eurodollars are not reacting as much as the long end of the curve. We're just gently moving upwards," said the trader.
